items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-07-21
items.q: Well, there are people like you and Dr. Rayburn and a few other contemporaries that I have just like, but we've been friends for years.

ctx.x: So you didn't have a specialty?

No. I mean there wasn't anything? No. Well, chemistry, I wasn't good in chemistry, I wasn't good in, what is that other thing, trigonometry. I could do a little algebra, I could read or write real good, but then again, I think I had, I was thinking about the Army, then I had the girls on my mind, then my mother took sick, just a little bit before I went into the Army. And her and my father was beginning to get back together, they developed a beautiful relationship, but they never officially lived in the same…
You know what Cosmo told me?

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: Some of my collections, I brought them to Dr. Rayburn to put into the archives

ctx.x: Yep. Some of my collections, I brought them to Dr. Rayburn to put into the archives that will live forever around here. So, like I said, we have done some things that I really feel proud of that I had lived at a time in history for the growth of the city of New Orleans in the greater metropolitan area where some positive things have been done between whites and blacks collectively, you know, because we...
You brought up, well, this may be a little much, we're just sort of crisscrossing here. Creoles, Creole blacks. What was your feeling about the relationship of the Creoles?
